plan_a_advantages: Includes a tempo run to improve lactate threshold and speed.
Features a longer run to build endurance and trail-specific durability.
Incorporates strength and mobility work for injury prevention and performance enhancement.
Has a more varied workout structure, promoting well-rounded development.
plan_b_advantages: Higher volume of easy runs may be beneficial for some athletes, particularly those new to trail running.
The focus on easy runs could be good for recovery if the athlete is coming off a period of intense training.
reasoning: Plan A is the better choice for an athlete aiming to become a faster trail runner. While both plans emphasize consistency, Plan A incorporates a tempo run and a longer run, which are crucial for developing speed and endurance specifically. Plan B relies solely on easy runs, which, while important for building a base, won't sufficiently challenge the athlete to improve their speed. The inclusion of strength and mobility work in Plan A also contributes to injury prevention and overall performance.
